statement: The initial pulse of Neanderthal-to-modern-human gene flow (roughly 50,000-60,000 years ago) was likely substantially higher than 5% of the genome, and was subsequently reduced by natural selection purging deleterious archaic variants over succeeding generations — which is why the Neanderthal-ancestry fraction observed in living genomes today (see claim_neanderthal_ancestry_by_population) is much lower than the original admixture event itself.

sources.citation: Harris, K. & Nielsen, R. "The Genetic Cost of Neanderthal Introgression." Genetics 203(2): 881-891.
sources.author: Harris & Nielsen
